items.title: Quasi-finiteness at a prime is preserved by a surjective change of the four rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a commutative square of rings with a surjective base change, quasi-finiteness at a prime descends to the corresponding prime of the target (statement lines 30509-30524). The proof does not estimate fibre dimensions: it uses the product decomposition of the fibre at the given point provided by quasi-finiteness, transports that decomposition along the base change, and shows the point remains isolated in the new fibre by a dimension zero argument (proof lines 30526-30556). Carrying the decomposition through the surjection is the step that makes the isolation visible. H2.
